A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NIAF research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original CALVIN and LIBERO evaluations, real-robot experiments, control trajectories, and ablation results.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds robot comparisons, Water Cup Transport trajectories, representation-fitting experiments, and a decoder-depth ablation.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 removes acceleration supervision and its numerically differentiated target from the stated real-world objective, retaining position supervision, velocity supervision, and jerk regularization. The SIREN architecture, grouped modulation, and inference procedure remain unchanged. This does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V2 retains CALVIN, LIBERO, and the four original real-world tasks, adding Water Cup Transport in Appendix B.2. Transporting water without spilling introduces a distinct smoothness-sensitive task requirement; the single-chunk fitting experiment is a diagnostic analysis rather than another benchmark.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds π0.5-BEAST and π0.5-OFT to the existing Shape Insertion and Towel Folding comparisons, which previously compared π0.5-NIAF only against vanilla π0.5. The comparator sets in the original simulation evaluations and Florence-2 robot comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark splits, evaluation counts, training budgets, and task-scoring procedures are retained. Added protocols compare Water Cup Transport policies under impedance control, fit a common 200-step trajectory with position and velocity objectives, and evaluate SIREN depths 2–4. These are supplementary protocols, not revisions to the original benchmark settings.

E4.justification: Appendices B.2–B.3 add substantial mechanism analyses: position-only versus position-plus-velocity supervision under a common controller, and SIREN versus B-spline fitting with and without SIREN jerk regularization. Table 6 additionally tests decoder depth. The earlier sampling-frequency, chunk-length, weight-group, and activation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Existing evaluation-trial counts remain unchanged, and the added analyses introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores and robot scores are retained, but the supporting results expand substantially. Figure 4 adds π0.5-BEAST/π0.5-OFT scores of 40/63 for Shape Insertion and 85/70 for Towel Folding. Table 6 adds depth results of 3.24, 4.47, and 4.20 for depths 2, 3, and 4; Figures 8–10 add qualitative control and fitting results.

T1.justification: The formal objective loses the acceleration-matching loss defined in v1 Equation 13 and its weighted contribution to the total loss. The action-representation definitions, derivative recursion, and impedance-control equation are otherwise retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The dynamics-supervision contribution is narrowed from constraining velocity, acceleration, and jerk to supervising velocity and regularizing jerk. Continuous action representation, backbone scalability, and impedance control remain the central contributions. Although the abstract now says 'strong results,' state-of-the-art claims remain in the introduction and experimental discussion.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning unchanged high-level reasoning/generalization, dependence on velocity feedback, and situations where simpler waypoint methods remain competitive. It also adds interpretations involving position–velocity cross-regularization, B-spline oversmoothing, possible forgetting after action-head replacement, and the capacity trade-off in decoder depth.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 newly specifies a three-hidden-layer, width-64 SIREN matching NIAF's decoder, along with the fitting experiment's spline configuration and objective. Section 4.3 explains the added π0.5 baseline-head implementations. Existing hyperparameter tables and demonstration-collection details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens action-representation coverage through LipVQ-VAE, ActionCodec, OAT, FASTER, OmniSAT, and RoboFlamingo, and adds a distinct discussion of latent-action approaches including Bu et al.'s UniVLA, SSM-VLA, and ALAM. This expands the research context beyond bibliographic updates to already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 refines the abstract, terminology, grammar, and method explanations while retaining the main narrative and section sequence. It adds limitations, acknowledgments, and an impact statement, and inserts two appendix subsections before the retained ablations. Much of the existing prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the architecture diagram, restructures Figure 4 into separate backbone panels, adds the trajectory and fitting displays in Figures 8–10, and expands Table 6 with a depth block. These are substantial display changes; the relocated original trajectory plots and rollout images are retained content.

improvement.justification: The common-controller Water Cup Transport comparison, controlled fitting analyses, and depth ablation strengthen evidence for mechanisms that v1 largely inferred from controller-confounded comparisons. Explicit limitations also improve scope calibration. The gain remains limited by qualitative and single-chunk evidence, and by retained statements that baselines cannot use impedance control despite their use of it in the new experiment.
